title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Cervical Cancer
summary: The HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project (HTMCP) cervical cancer cohort was assembled to study how HIV infection shapes cervical carcinoma in a population where both diseases are common. It is one of very few NCI-supported genomic cohorts whose participants are almost entirely Black African women recruited outside the United States, and that makes it structurally different from every other cervical cancer resource in the portfolio. The cohort carries whole genome sequencing on 124 cases, RNA sequencing on 123, methylation arrays on 120, microRNA on 118, and both histopathology and radiology images on 211 - an unusually complete multimodal picture for a cohort of this size and origin.
one_liner: 212 cervical carcinomas from Ugandan women, 98% Black African and enriched for HIV infection - the largest genomically characterized cervical cancer cohort from sub-Saharan Africa, with ECOG status on 99% of cases, treatment outcome on 68%, and a derivable follow-up time for every single case.

useful_for.question: Does HPV clade shape the tumor epigenome and transcriptome differently in an African cohort than in the predominantly North American and European cohorts that define current cervical cancer subtypes?
useful_for.rationale: Methylation arrays are available on 120 cases and RNA sequencing on 123, on the same tumors as whole genome sequencing that can be used to type and subclassify the integrated HPV. This is the design the marker paper used, and the cohort is large enough to repeat it with different clade groupings or to test subtype assignments derived from TCGA-CESC against an independent, differently constituted population.
useful_for.statistical_note: Analyses restricted to the intersection of methylation and expression leave roughly 118 cases; clade subgroups below about 25 cases will not support multiple-testing corrected genome-wide comparisons.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Do molecular subtypes derived from predominantly white cohorts transfer to Black African patients, or do they misclassify tumors in this population?
useful_for.rationale: 207 of 212 cases are recorded as Black or African American, making this the only cohort in this corpus where a non-white group constitutes more than half the participants. Expression and methylation data allow subtype classifiers trained on TCGA to be applied directly, and classifier failure is itself the finding.
useful_for.statistical_note: Because the cohort is nearly homogeneous by race, this is a transfer-validation design rather than a within-cohort disparities comparison; there is no internal white comparison group.

useful_for.question: Which molecular features are associated with performance status and with response to chemoradiation in a setting where platinum-based chemoradiation is the dominant treatment?
useful_for.rationale: ECOG performance status is informative on 98.6% of cases, which is exceptional - most GDC projects record it for none. Treatment type is populated for every case, therapeutic agents for 29.7% (cisplatin, paclitaxel and carboplatin are the commonest), and a treatment outcome field is populated for 67.9%. Together these support a response analysis that is impossible in most cohorts of this size.
useful_for.statistical_note: Roughly 144 cases have a populated treatment outcome. Response categories are unevenly distributed and the outcome field is one-to-many, so collapse to a binary responder definition per case before modeling and pre-register that definition.

useful_for.question: How do survival patterns in this cohort compare with cervical cancer cohorts from high-income settings, given a median follow-up of only 13.2 months?
useful_for.rationale: Vital status is informative for 100% of cases and follow-up time is computable, giving a usable overall survival endpoint. The short follow-up is itself scientifically interesting because it reflects real-world attrition in the setting where the cohort was recruited.
useful_for.statistical_note: Median follow-up is 13.2 months and the maximum is 32.7, so late events are not observed. Report restricted mean survival time or landmark analyses rather than median overall survival, and do not compare medians directly against cohorts with five-year follow-up.

useful_for.question: Can radiology and histopathology images from this cohort be used to build or validate imaging models on a population that is absent from almost every public imaging training set?
useful_for.rationale: Histopathology and radiology are both available for 211 of 212 cases, alongside the molecular data. Imaging models trained largely on North American and European cohorts have documented performance gaps on under-represented populations, and this is one of the few resources that permits an external check.
useful_for.statistical_note: Suitable for external validation rather than primary training; 211 cases is small for training a deep model from scratch.

limitations.statement: Tumor stage is not populated for any case in the GDC harmonized clinical records - both AJCC pathologic stage and AJCC clinical stage are empty for all 212 cases. Since stage is the dominant prognostic factor in cervical cancer, any survival model built from these records alone is unadjusted for the single most important covariate.
affected_analyses: Any comparison of outcomes against staged cohorts
limitations.mitigation: The marker publication reports stage information, so it exists outside the harmonized records. Obtain it from the publication's supplementary material or through the dbGaP phenotype files before claiming any stage-adjusted result.

limitations.statement: HIV status is not available as a structured field, despite being the organizing scientific rationale for the cohort. Neither CD4 count nor antiretroviral therapy history appears in the harmonized clinical records.
limitations.mitigation: Request the full phenotype file through dbGaP. Do not assume HIV positivity for all participants: the project name describes the study population, not a guarantee about every case.

limitations.statement: Median follow-up is 13.2 months with a maximum of 32.7, derivable for all 212 cases. Events accumulate over a much longer horizon in cervical cancer, so the observed survival experience is heavily right-censored.
limitations.mitigation: Use restricted mean survival time over a horizon the data support, or landmark analysis. State the follow-up distribution explicitly in any comparison.

limitations.statement: Ethnicity is recorded as unknown or not reported for 111 of 212 cases, and the cohort is drawn from a single geographic setting. Findings describe Ugandan cervical cancer patients and should not be generalised to Black populations elsewhere, whose exposure and treatment contexts differ substantially.
affected_analyses: Generalization to African-ancestry populations outside Uganda
limitations.mitigation: Frame results as specific to this cohort and setting, and report the recruitment context alongside any ancestry claim.

access_steps.detail: The Nature Genetics paper describes the recruitment setting, HPV typing approach and the clinical variables that exist outside the harmonized records. It will tell you whether the variables your analysis needs are obtainable at all.

access_steps.action: Explore the open-access files without any approval
access_steps.detail: 2,457 of 7,160 files are open. Derived expression, copy number and methylation products are enough to scope the analysis and check that the cohort fits before you invest in an access request.
access_steps.cli_snippet:
# Open-access file manifest for this project, no credentials required
curl -s 'https://api.gdc.cancer.gov/files' \
  --get \
  --data-urlencode 'filters={"op":"and","content":[
    {"op":"in","content":{"field":"cases.project.project_id","value":["CGCI-HTMCP-CC"]}},
    {"op":"in","content":{"field":"access","value":["open"]}}]}' \
  --data-urlencode 'fields=file_id,file_name,data_category,data_type' \
  --data-urlencode 'size=2000&format=TSV' > htmcp_cc_open_files.tsv

access_steps.action: Submit a dbGaP data access request for the controlled tier
access_steps.detail: Needed for whole genome sequencing and any sequence-level analysis. You will need an eRA Commons account and your institutional signing official. Request the full phenotype file at the same time - that is where stage and HIV-related variables are most likely to live.
Once approved, use the GDC Data Transfer Tool with your token. Do not put the token on a command line or into a script that is committed anywhere.

open_questions: HIV status, CD4 count and antiretroviral therapy history are central to this cohort's scientific value but are not exposed as structured fields in the GDC harmonized clinical records. Confirm with the CGCI data access committee whether they are available in the dbGaP phenotype files before planning an HIV-stratified analysis.

Stage is unpopulated in GDC for all 212 cases. The marker paper reports stage distribution, so it exists somewhere; confirm whether it can be obtained from the supplementary tables or only through controlled access.
